newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Eyewitness Udugodage Mahindapala, giving evidence at the Magistrate's inquiry into the death of Nalanda Ellawala, said he tried to hold on to former United National Party (UNP) mayor of Ratnapura Mahinda Ratnatilaka who had a gun in his hands, and pleaded with him not to shoot Ellawala. Ellawala, a ruling People's Alliance (PA) member of parliament, was gunned down in Ratnapura in central Sri Lanka, on Tuesday.
Local government polls set for March 21, says Elections Commissioner.
Tension in Ratnapura after slaying of Nalanda Ellawala on Tuesday. Ten shops burnt, and curfew reimposed on Wednesday.

Nalanda Ellawala staggered away from UNP member of parliament Susantha Punchinilame holding his stomach, when Mahinda Ratnatilaka tried to shoot him, said eyewitness Udugodage Mahindapala, at Wednesday's Magistrate's inquiry.

Government will not postpone local government polls under any circumstances, says PA general secretary and senior government minister, D.M.Jayaratne. The government has accused the UNP of trying to use "terror tactics" to disrupt polls.
President Kumaratunga appoints special police team headed by senior deputy inspector general, A.J.Iddamalgoda, to investigate slaying of Nalanda Ellawala.
Local goverbnment elections on March 21, says elections commissioner.
Nalanda Ellawala died of gunshot injuries to the liver, lungs, intestines and stomach, says judicial medical officer, Dr A.J Alwis.
Twelve recognised political parties and 133 independent groups to contest March 21 local government polls.
